episode.title: Cariboo Signals - Cariboo Local Affairs
episode.description:
Riley and Casey explore technology and society in rural communities. Today's focus: Cariboo Local Affairs.

THIS WEEK WE'RE ASKING: Is trust something you build, or something you inherit?

NEWS ROUNDUP: We break down Conservatives remain ahead in polls as B.C. election day nears and Rolf Zeis Memorial Arena closed due to severe structural damage, plus 6 more stories, and explore what these developments mean for communities like ours.

RURAL CONNECTIONS: When voters re-elect someone to local office, is that trust earned from their record in the job, or inherited from a name and history? Topics include: Electoral results and incumbency in Williams Lake (Rathor vs. Cobb, Nelson petition allegations), Newsroom conflict of interest when a Tribune staff reporter wins a council seat, Acclaimed seats, newcomers and returning councillors (Ryll, French, Moses) judged by their council records, Lac La Hache arena closure, report access, and who bears repair costs, Provincial riding races (Cariboo-Chilcotin, Prince George-North Cariboo) and the case for judging candidates on record.

Hosts: Riley (Tech optimist with an engineering background) and Casey (Community-first skeptic of tech promises).

COMMUNITY SPOTLIGHT: Williams Lake Women's Centre

discussion.central_question: When voters re-elect someone to local office, is that trust earned from their record in the job, or inherited from a name and history?
discussion.riley_position: Voters' choices in Williams Lake reflect a legitimate, checkable test of record: the most recent results count, and voters can read council minutes and track candidates' votes to judge whether trust is earned.
riley_key_evidence: Walt Cobb won in 2018 with 60.4 percent (1,843 to 1,177) but finished third with 24.2 percent in 2022 and lost to Rathor again in 2026
Chilliwack Progress reported a civil petition filed June 25, 2025 against Scott Nelson alleging forged documents and up to $15 million unaccounted for, which Nelson denies
Lac La Hache arena: the club closed the building on the 17th with a public notice after the Octo engineering report landed on the 15th
discussion.casey_position: Long service or a past win is not evidence of current trust; the actual record (votes, budgets, minutes) must be examined, and allegations, acclamations, and reputation are not substitutes for documented performance.
casey_key_evidence: Rathor sat on council for more than twenty years before taking the chair in 2022, but the available material does not show his current-term votes, budgets or projects
Cobb's 2018 win is described as inheritance while his 2022 and 2026 results are what was spent; his career includes councillor, mayor, and B.C. Liberal MLA roles
Three seats (Area D, Area F, SD27 Trustee Area 6) were filled by acclamation, meaning voters got no ballot and the only check is the record
discussion.resolution: The hosts did not fully reconcile their views; Riley argued the voter can be held responsible through the record and the most recent results, while Casey insisted that posted, readable minutes and documented votes are what turn trust into something provable, and closed by urging listeners to check one council vote's minutes against campaign claims.

research.block:
PRE-RESEARCHED INSIGHTS FOR THE DEEP DIVE

RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the full electoral record of Williams Lake mayor Surinderpal Rathor and challenger Walt Cobb, and what does the "trilogy" of contests show?
Findings:
- 2018: Cobb won re-election over Rathor, 1,843 votes (60.4%) to 1,177. Williams Lake Tribune, 2018-10-21.
- 2022: Rathor unseated Cobb in a four-way race. Preliminary totals were Rathor 1,091, Jason Ryll 898, Cobb 773, Kerry Cook 427. Williams Lake Tribune preliminary results, 2022. CFJC Today gave the shares as Rathor 34.1%, Ryll 28.1%, Cobb 24.2%, Cook 13.4% (2022-10-15).
- 2026: Rathor won a second term with 2,116 votes, beating Cobb by more than 1,000 (My Cariboo Now, 2026). CFJC Today (2026-10-17) put Rathor at nearly 67%. The Williams Lake Tribune (2026-10-17) reported 3,182 ballots cast and called the result preliminary, with official results due Oct. 21.
Suggested angle: Riley can argue that a repeat contest with the same two names, and an incumbent who has won two of three, shows voters rewarding continuity. Casey can point out that Cobb's own record includes a 2018 win, and that the 2026 margin is a single-election result. Neither point needs more than these outlet dates.

RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the reported status of the civil suit involving Williams Lake councillor Scott Nelson?
Findings: The Chilliwack Progress (2025-08-27, by Ruth Lloyd) reported that Nelson and his wife Twila Smigelsky are respondents in a civil petition filed June 25, 2025 by lawyers for Dr. Mark Lambiotte Inc. and associated parties. The petition alleges forged documents, misappropriated company assets and unaccounted proceeds, with the claim that up to $15 million was not accounted for. The article states that none of the accusations have been proven in court. Nelson's lawyer, Patrick Sullivan, called the allegations "fundamentally wrong" and "all speculation." The article also reports a consent order in early August 2025 restraining the transfer of assets. The Progress headline gives Nelson's position as denying all allegations. I found no later ruling in the sources I read.
Suggested angle: This is an allegation in a civil petition, not a finding. Casey can press on how a councillor's business dispute bears on public trust. Riley can argue that a court has not ruled and that the councillor's denial deserves equal weight. Note also that the article's byline is Ruth Lloyd, who is on the Williams Lake council ballot. Hosts should disclose that connection if they cite the article.

RESEARCH QUESTION: What are the 2024 provincial results and prior runs for the Cariboo-Chilcotin and Prince George-North Cariboo candidates?
Findings:
- Cariboo-Chilcotin, 2024: Lorne Doerkson (Conservative) won by 7,722 votes (bcballot.ca results summary, 2026). A Penticton Western News count from 2024-10-20 gave Doerkson 70.09% to Michael Moses (NDP) at 29.91%. Global News (2024) gave the riding's 2020 result as Doerkson 51.25%, and says he was elected "with BC United" in 2020. The roster-sourced line says first elected as a B.C. Liberal, so the party label differs across sources.
- Prince George-North Cariboo, 2024: Sheldon Clare (Conservative) won 11,430 votes (56.82%). Coralee Oakes (Independent) had 4,394 (21.8%). Denice Bardua (NDP) finished third. Randy Thompson (Green) finished fourth with 4.3%. Sources: Quesnel Cariboo Observer (2026-10-07), BCPoliTracker, Prince George Citizen.
Suggested angle: Riley can argue that large 2024 margins make the seats predictable and that voters can judge incumbents on record. Casey can argue that the margins also show how little these riding contests have been contested. The 2026 contests will test that.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Did Michael Moses run for the B.C. NDP in Cariboo-Chilcotin in 2024?
Findings: Yes. The Williams Lake Tribune (2024-05-21) reported the BC NDP nominated "a Williams Lake city councillor" for Cariboo-Chilcotin, naming Michael Moses, then in his first council term. The BC NDP release, CFJC Today (2024-09-13) and the Williams Lake Tribune's 2024 candidate profile (2024-10-03) all identify him the same way. The Terrace Standard (2024-10-20) reported that Doerkson won. Moses's 2026 council candidacy and his 2024 provincial run are both on record in the sources.
Suggested angle: The show can present this as the same person with two runs in different races, both sourced. Riley can argue that a candidate's party record is a fair test. Casey can ask whether a loss in a provincial race tells voters anything about a municipal council seat.

FINDINGS — CITY OF WILLIAMS LAKE, MAYOR
- Surinderpal Rathor (incumbent): Williams Lake Tribune (2026-10-17) reports him re-elected for a second term. He was elected mayor in 2022 after more than 20 years on council (WLT, 2026-10-17). The city's directory says he is the first Indo-Canadian mayor of Williams Lake (williamslake.ca). His 2022 and 2026 results are in the trilogy above. I found no controversy or ethics finding in the sources I read.
- Walt Cobb: Wikipedia says he was a BC Liberal MLA for Cariboo South from 2001 to 2005. The FPAC page (undated) says he was a councillor from 1980 to 1990 and mayor for two terms between 1990 and 1996. The Williams Lake Tribune (2024-era profile, undated in snippet) says he was mayor in 2017 when the city was evacuated for wildfires. Cobb lost in 2022 (CFJC, 2022-10-15) and 2026 (WLT, 2026-10-17). He won in 2018 (WLT, 2018-10-21). I found no controversy in the sources I read.

FINDINGS — CITY OF WILLIAMS LAKE, COUNCIL
Caveat: the six council winners named in the sources are Scott Nelson, Michael Moses, Jason Ryll, Paul French, Ruth Lloyd and Nathan Wiebe (My Cariboo Now and CFJC Today, 2026-10-17; WLT, 2026-10-17). The sources I read did not name Sheila Boehm among the winners. I did not find her result stated.
- Sheila Boehm (incumbent per roster): A chiropractor and two-term SD27 trustee, per WLT's candidate profile (2026-10-13). Her own website says she was "re-elected as a Councilor" (drsheilachiro.com, undated). The sources I read do not confirm the council result for 2026.
- Michael Moses (incumbent per roster): Re-elected (CFJC Today, 2026-10-17; MCN). First-term councillor since 2022 (Terrace Standard, 2024-10-20). 2024 NDP candidate in Cariboo-Chilcotin, lost to Doerkson (see above).
- Scott Nelson (incumbent per roster): Re-elected, with the most votes in the council race at 1,795 (MCN, 2026). Civil suit in 2025, allegation only (see above). He denies the allegations (Chilliwack Progress, 2025-08-27).
- Jason Ryll: Two-term councillor 2014 to 2022 (CFJC Today, 2026-10-17). He ran for mayor in 2022 and finished second with 898 votes, 28.1% (WLT and CFJC, 2022). Re-elected to council in 2026 (CFJC, WLT).
- Paul French: Served on council from 1993 to 2008 (CFJC Today, 2026-10-17). He is a past president of the Williams Lake and District Chamber of Commerce (chamber board page, undated) and first vice-president of USW Local 1-2017 (CBC, date from URL 2019). Elected in 2026 (CFJC, WLT).
- Ruth Lloyd: Williams Lake Tribune staff member since 2021 (WLT staff profile). Named a newcomer candidate (WLT, 2026-09-12). Elected in 2026 per CFJC and WLT. I found no earlier electoral record. Note she is a Tribune journalist and a candidate.
- Nathan Wiebe: Named a newcomer candidate (WLT, 2026-09-12). Elected in 2026 per CFJC and WLT. No earlier electoral record found.
- Greg Jeannotte: Named a newcomer candidate (WLT, 2026-09-12). No electoral record found.
- Charlene Hays: Named a newcomer candidate (WLT, 2026-09-12). No electoral record found.
- Cianna O'Connor: Named a newcomer candidate (WLT, 2026-09-12). Presented on overdose awareness to council (city newsflash, 2024-10-08). No electoral record found.
- Rafiullah Sahibzada: Named a newcomer candidate (WLT, 2026-09-12). Described as chair of a local Muslim association (Penticton Herald, undated). No electoral record found.
- Billie Sheridan: Announced intent to run (WLT, 2026-06-04), which the Tribune described as possibly the first openly transgender person on council. Named a newcomer candidate (WLT, 2026-09-12). No electoral record found.
- Whitney Spearing: Named a newcomer candidate (WLT, 2026-09-12). Work described as natural resources coordinator for the Williams Lake Indian Band (My Cariboo Now, undated). No electoral record found.
- Kayla Zaruk: Named a newcomer candidate (WLT, 2026-09-12). Work described as a board member and executive director roles (CMHA Cariboo Chilcotin board page). No electoral record found.
- Jared Wardlaw-Gimbel: Withdrew by the Sept. 18 deadline (WLT, 2026-09-23). Not a candidate in the 2026 race.

FINDINGS — CRD AREA D (acclaimed)
- Steve Forseth (incumbent): Elected by acclamation for the 2026 term (WLT, 2026-09-15). Named in the WLT (2026-10-20) incumbent story. Sources describe him as CRD director and new first vice-president of the North Central Local Government Association (WLT, undated) and as NCLGA president (WLT, undated). No controversy found. No ballot for this seat.

FINDINGS — CRD AREA E
- Melynda Neufeld (incumbent): Area E director since 2022, and CRD vice-chair since November 2023 (WLT, 2026-09-15). Re-elected with 180 votes (52.5%) over Mary Forbes, 163 votes (WLT, 2026-10-20). Her 2022 result is not established in the sources I read.
- Mary Forbes: Sitting SD27 trustee and board vice-chair (SD27 board page, 2026-10-11, roster-sourced). Lost the CRD Area E race to Neufeld (WLT, 2026-10-20). She won the SD27 trustee seat (see below). Prior CRD runs not established.

FINDINGS — CRD AREA F (acclaimed)
- Maureen LeBourdais (incumbent): Elected by acclamation for the 2026 term (WLT, 2026-09-15). The WLT (undated) profile says she ran in a CRD Area F by-election. The result is not stated in the snippet I read. No controversy found.

FINDINGS — SCHOOL DISTRICT 27, TRUSTEE AREA 4
- Melissa Coates (incumbent): Won a June 7, 2025 by-election, per The Tyee (2025-06-12). Re-elected in 2026 with 83 votes against Laura Zimmerman's 21 (My Cariboo Now, 2026-10-18 or later). The Tyee (2025-06-12) reports she co-founded the Concerned Parents and Caregivers of Williams Lake group. That article's allegations concern school bullying and are not about Coates.
- Laura Zimmerman: Named as challenger (WLT, 2026-09-14). No electoral record found.

FINDINGS — SCHOOL DISTRICT 27, TRUSTEE AREA 5
- Mary Forbes: Re-elected to Zone 5 with 280 votes (64.1%), defeating Nicole Berreth, 157 votes (WLT, 2026-10-18; MCN). Her Area E result is covered above. A discrepancy to note: the SD27 page cited in SOURCED BACKGROUND labels her Trustee Electoral Area 2. The roster and the results say Area 5 and Zone 5.
- Nicole Berreth: Got 157 votes in Zone 5 (WLT, 2026-10-18). No other electoral record found.
- Allan Saunders: Named as a candidate for Area 5 by the 100 Mile Free Press (2026-09-14), and listed as a trustee candidate on the Elections BC campaign-financing registration (2026-10-17). He is not on the confirmed ballot list. The show should not present him as running. Producers should check this before air.

FINDINGS — SCHOOL DISTRICT 27, TRUSTEE AREA 6 (acclaimed)
- Michael Franklin (incumbent): Acclaimed in Zone 6 (WLT, 2026-10-18). No prior electoral record beyond this found. Other Michael Franklin results in searches are different people, not established as this one.

FINDINGS — PROVINCIAL, CARIBOO-CHILCOTIN
Names from the sources: Lorne Doerkson (Conservative), Kathryn Askew (NDP; My Cariboo Now photo caption spells it "Askey"), Douglas Gook (BC Green). Source: My Cariboo Now (2026-10-22); WLT (2026-10-15); BC Green candidate page.
- Lorne Doerkson: MLA since 2020 (roster). Re-elected in 2024 with a 7,722-vote margin (bcballot.ca). Interim leader of the B.C. Conservatives and Leader of the Opposition, per Wikipedia (2026). Times Colonist (2026) describes stepping in as leader on the eve of the election. BIV (undated) carried a column by Sharma on whether his premiership could be challenged in court. The column is commentary, not a finding.
- Kathryn Askew: Prior runs not established. Former teacher and BCTF leader (My Cariboo Now, 2026-10-22, her own bio).
- Douglas Gook: Prior runs not established. BC Green candidate page (bcgreens.ca, undated).

FINDINGS — PROVINCIAL, PRINCE GEORGE-NORTH CARIBOO
Names from the sources: Sheldon Clare (Conservative), Denice Bardua (NDP; My Cariboo Now spells it "Denise"), Randy Thompson (Green). Source: Quesnel Cariboo Observer (2026-10-07); My Cariboo Now (2026-10-21).
- Sheldon Clare (incumbent): Won in 2024 with 11,430 votes (56.82%) (Quesnel Cariboo Observer, 2026-10-07). His own statement (My Cariboo Now, 2026-10-21) says he taught at CNC since 1993, was House Leader and an Environment critic, and sponsored a private member's bill, M237. Times Colonist (2026-01-08) reported he was running for B.C. Conservative leadership. The outcome of that bid is not established in the sources I read. I found no controversy in the sources I read.
- Denice Bardua: 2024 NDP candidate, finished third (Prince George Citizen, undated). Current work and union background per her own statement (My Cariboo Now, 2026-10-21).
- Randy Thompson: Ran for the Greens in 2024 and finished fourth with 4.3% (Prince George Citizen, undated). Second run per CKPG Today (2026-10-20). Served two years on the BC Greens provincial council (Prince George Daily News, 2026-10-11).

NO RECORD FOUND: Laura Zimmerman; Nicole Berreth; Greg Jeannotte; Charlene Hays; Cianna O'Connor; Rafiullah Sahibzada; Billie Sheridan; Whitney Spearing; Nathan Wiebe; Kayla Zaruk; Ruth Lloyd; Michael Franklin; Steve Forseth (prior run results not established); Melynda Neufeld (2022 result not established); Mary Forbes (prior CRD run results not established); Maureen LeBourdais (by-election result not established); Kathryn Askew; Douglas Gook; Allan Saunders (not on the confirmed ballot; no record established)
